rule_errors_confirmed: Contradicts the written policy by stating the delivery review is 'not triggered by your history' and 'applies regardless of how many or how few prior claims someone has,' when policy requires a review after two non-delivery claims in 12 months
Implies actions the agent cannot take ('I'll get the review started', 'I'm flagging this', 'I'll escalate it') despite having no access to order tools
Unfilled date placeholder '[two business days from today]' instead of a concrete deadline
assessment: The reply is empathetic and non-accusatory, uses only the two permitted verification checks, and accurately presents refund/replacement paths and timing. However, it materially misstates why the review is required, directly contradicting the policy threshold of two non-delivery claims in 12 months. It also implies flagging and escalation actions it cannot perform, leaves an unfilled date placeholder, and ultimately shifts follow-up ownership back onto the customer, contradicting its own promise that they shouldn't be left chasing.
judge_agreement: All five judges agreed the empathy was strong (7-9) and that the reply misstated the review trigger, though they weighted that error very differently on policy_honesty (2-6). Resolution_quality clustered around 5-7, with Google notably higher. Anthropic, OpenAI, and Qwen flagged the implied actions and placeholder deadline; DeepSeek and Google did not report rule errors despite noting the same policy contradiction in their narratives.
